issue.title: %w:<session> waiters release mid gate follow-up launch: settlement pre-stamps gate_followup_outcome=failed, resolver reads it as no successor

task_type_fields.impact: Every `%w:<session>` (or fork/identity wait that uses the session aggregate) on a session whose plan gate gets approved is very likely released at approval time instead of when the session's code/monitor/retry turns are done. Agents then run against unlanded work from the session they waited on. In this case 11q.w0 planned and coded while 11q's coder was still running. Fix directions: don't persist a terminal-looking outcome before the launch in settle mode (Rust `decide_gate_followup` and/or `apply_decision`), and/or treat a gate with `gate_next_action` plus a live `gate_followup_attempt_*` as pending in `turn_followup_handoff_agent`. Add a regression test for a mid-launch approved plan gate that keeps a session waiter parked.
task_type_fields.repro:
Observed 2026-10-19 (bob-cli): `11q.w0--plan` launched with `%w:11q` and was released at 09:44:05 by `wait_checks` (`wait_dependencies_satisfied_at` = 09:43:55.21, the gate's first `done.json`). That was while `11q--gate` was mid follow-up launch and before `11q--code` existed (artifact dir 20261019094413, created 09:44:13). The 11q session was nowhere near done: code → monitor (failed) → `11q--1` were still to come.

Root cause (two parts):
1. `gate_turn/handoff_launch.py::launch_or_record_followup` runs `classify_gate_handoff(mode="settle")` *before* launching. On the normal settle input (gate `answered`, follow-up requested, no outcome/attempt recorded) the Rust classifier returns `persist_outcome: "failed"`, `disposition: "interrupted"`, `launch_allowed: true`. `apply_decision` writes `gate_followup_outcome: "failed"` to the gate's agent_meta.json. `launched` replaces it only after the launch returns, about 18 s later (`wait_for_starter` + spawn).
2. `core/wait_dependency_resolution/_artifact_state.py::turn_followup_handoff_agent` returns `<pending-turn-followup>` only when `followup_outcome is None`. With `"failed"` it returns None, so `_agent_session_entity` sees `handoffs_present=True` and resolves the session. The gate's own done.json write wakes the `wait_checks` tick, so the tick almost always lands inside the window. The confirmation rescan only catches new member dirs, which don't exist yet.

Repro: rebuild a WaitDependencyIndex from `~/.sase/projects`, rewound to the window (gate done.json without `gate_followup_*`, no 11q--code dir), then call `dependency_resolution_status(index, ["11q"], self_artifact_dir=<waiter>)`. With the gate meta's `gate_followup_outcome` absent the result is `waiting`. With it set to `"failed"` the result is `resolved`. Separately, `classify_gate_handoff(meta, mode="settle", already_settled=False, followup_requested=True, successor_evidence={})` returns `persist_outcome: "failed"`. Full write-up: the research report in the attached artifact ref.

issue.creation_reason: Found while explaining why 11q.w0 started before 11q finished. Session waits can release at plan-gate approval instead of when the session completes.

payload.description: Same gate follow-up outcome fields (gate_followup_outcome); sase-wp is about silent launch failures, this is a premature 'failed' value read by wait resolution
